title: t5 (null-weight-shuffled): the model does not perform the behaviour; no circuit claimed
label: null finding: no behaviour, no mechanism
behavior: BOS + 5 tokens from 5 symbols (bo, fe, ka, lu, ri); one symbol is output at the last position. Dataset task 'bench', path benchmarks/glassbox-bench/seed-1/tasks/t5.
summary: On local-full (full precision) the loaded 1-layer, 2-head, d_model=29 checkpoint agrees with the dataset's answers only at chance: 0.203 on 128 prompts (E0002) and 0.200 on 400 independent prompts (E0003), where chance for 5 symbols is 0.20. The mean logit difference between the dataset answer and the foil is about zero (-1.0 and +0.17) with a standard deviation of about 13-14, and the model sometimes predicts PAD, which is never an answer. The investigation was stopped at step 1: there is no behaviour to explain, so no heads or MLP layers are claimed, no predict() was written and verify_hypothesis was not run. Status: no mechanism found (not verified, by design).

claims.text: The loaded model does not perform the behaviour: clean accuracy against the dataset answers is 0.203 on n=128, indistinguishable from chance (0.20). The pre-registered prediction of accuracy >= 0.95 was refuted. Backend: local-full, full precision.

The chance-level result replicates on an independent, larger sample: accuracy 0.200 on n=400 (pre-registered band 0.12-0.30, confirmed); mean logit difference 0.17 with std 14.0, so there is no systematic preference for the dataset answer.
Because there is no behaviour, no attention head or MLP layer is claimed to implement anything; the circuit is empty.

limitations: Only baselines were run (3 of 25 experiments). No patching, ablation or attention analysis was done because there was no behaviour to localise.
verify_hypothesis was not run: there is no algorithm or circuit to verify.

The label rule (output = fixed permutation of the 3rd input token) was read off 64 examples in an exploratory dataset inspection (E0001) and was not tested on held-out labels; it is an observation about the labels, not a claim about this model.

The task text says the dataset answers are the model's own outputs, yet the loaded checkpoint disagrees with them 80% of the time. The investigation name suggests the weights in memory are a shuffled null version; this was not independently checked.
open_questions: Does the loaded model compute some other deterministic function of the input (it is deterministic by construction)? Not investigated: it would not be the behaviour defined by the dataset.
Is the mismatch between dataset answers and the loaded weights intended (null control) or a loading issue?
overall_status: unverified (no verification run) · null finding: no behaviour, no mechanism

refuted_predictions.hypothesis: The model performs its behaviour reliably on the bench dataset (answers are its own outputs), with a clear logit margin between its answer and the answer for the corrupt prompt.

prediction.statement: Clean accuracy at least 95% on 128 prompts
